findings.location: sections/concise/10-commentary.tex lines 210-213 ('and Ambrose says that faith is pressed when we believe in Christ crucified. By Ambrose's account, then, the Thessalonians' faith was pressed both in what they believed and by the persecution that followed.'); the expansive study's source sentence at sections/20-crushed-seed.tex lines 213-215
findings.problem: The conclusion uses one verb for two things Ambrose keeps apart. At Exp. in Lucam VII.179 (tracked Wikisource artifact book-7-html-895ee72a) he writes 'Sed alias teritur fides, alias premitur, alias seminatur': faith is ground in one way, pressed in another and sown in another. Adversity grinds it ('si teratur adversis', VII.178, which this commentary renders 'if it is ground by adversity' at lines 34-36). Belief in the crucified presses it ('Premitur fides, cum crucifixum credimus Christum', VII.181, rendered at lines 43-44 and 211-212). On Ambrose's account, then, the persecution ground the Thessalonians' faith rather than pressed it. This round's SYN-010 repair makes the slip easier to see, because the sentence before now defines Ambrose's pressing as belief in Christ crucified. Elsewhere 'adversity presses it' (04-themes.tex lines 18-19) is a loose rendering that does no harm on its own, because it is not set against Ambrose's other verb. In substance both acts work on faith in Ambrose's account, so the reader is not materially misled. This is a single instance, and the concise study carries the accepted study's wording faithfully.
findings.required_result: Use Ambrose's own verb for each act. Commentary lines 212-213: 'By Ambrose's account, then, the Thessalonians' faith was pressed in what they believed and ground by the persecution that followed.' For the study owner at its next revision, sections/20-crushed-seed.tex lines 213-215: 'On Ambrose's account, then, the Thessalonians' faith was pressed in what they believed and ground by the persecution that followed.'

findings.problem: Carried forward from iterations 0 and 1. It was re-read this round and is still true, since the expansive study is unchanged here. The run cites '(Hom. in 1 Thess. 1)' at line 183, after the persecution sentence. It then gives the affliction-and-joy sentence, the Three Children and the imitators of the Lord without a citation, and closes with '(Hom. 2)' at line 191, after the remark on verse 8. The tracked NPNF I.13 text (ccel-npnf113-text-54274dd9) puts all three of those uncited passages in Homily I, which begins at physical line 29098: the imitators at 29262 and the Three Children at 29279. Only the verse-8 remark ('sounded out', 29520) belongs to Homily II, which begins at 29497. A reader reasonably takes everything after the first citation as Homily 2. The concise study cites Homily 1 correctly, so this stage has nothing to repair.

summary: Artifact: the concise study (synthesis.tex: sections/concise/01-inventory, 02-overview, generated page 2, 04-themes, 10-commentary, 90-apparatus), with generation-metadata.tex and research/production-review.md, against the accepted expansive study and the cited loci; REVIEW_SCOPE read in full, the rest of the concise study read for context. SYN-009 is repaired: line 293 now reads 'Three medieval commentators on the Mass who expound these chants read them as one sequence', which the records support (Rupert XII.23, Sicard VIII.23, and Durandus VI.140, re-read in the tracked 1612 OCR at lines 17384-17440: the conversion of the Jews at the end, Joseph, Introit, Gradual, Offertory and Communion), and line 444 restores 'cited here'. The SYN-010 advisory is cleared: Douay-Rheims Acts 17:3 reads 'the Christ was to suffer', and Ambrose VII.181 has 'Premitur fides, cum crucifixum credimus Christum' (tracked Wikisource text). production-review.md's iteration-2 entry matches the files, including the net three words, and the new contribution line follows the run's form at the stage's declared effort. Each interpretation's answer can be recovered from the concise prose alone. In the first, the least seed becomes a tree by giving out its strength when it is crushed: Christ seized, buried and risen (Hilary, Ambrose, Chrysologus), and faith ground by adversity (Ambrose), seen in a church pressed first and then heard of everywhere. In the second, the leaven is love (Augustine, Bede) or teaching (Jerome, Ambrose). Bede's sentence joins them as commanded love working through the whole person until the whole mind is changed, perfected only where God is all in all. In the third, deliverance is sung as done because what God foretold is as certain as the past (Augustine) and sin, its cause, is already removed (Aquinas). God urges prayer for what he promised so that it may be deserved (Jerome; Hilary's faith that prays to be heard), and the whole is leavened when Christ comes (Chrysologus). Page-2 lookup on the generated table: the Communion, Mark 11:24, gives 'Narrated event: Jesus teaches faith and prayer; Bethany to Jerusalem, before the Passion' paired with 'A.D. 29 (derived; Maas's chronology)', and Mark's composition, Rome traditionally, with proposals spanning A.D. 38-70. The Epistle, 1 Thess 1:2-10, gives Corinth to Thessalonica, with proposals spanning A.D. 52-54. Each pairing is found in its own row without crossing another column's paragraph, so the page is usable. Spot-checked at the tracked loci, all exact: NPNF Chrysostom (Hom. in Mt. 46.2-3, 47.1, 67.2; Hom. in 1 Thess. 1 and 2, with the homily boundaries) and NPNF Augustine (En. in Ps. 43.1, 43.6-7, 77, 84); Quaest. Ev. I.11-12; Bede, In Marc. III; Ambrose VII.178-190; Chrysologus, Sermo 99 (the measures as Law, Prophets and Gospels); Aquinas, Super Mt. c. 13 (Venice OCR). Physical pages: make doc into this review's scratch gave 12 pages. The settled aux is byte-identical to the author proof's (sha256 4df07415...). It places the inventory, the overview and its four sense markers on p1, the chronology on p2, the themes on p3-4 and the commentary's start on p5, with no overfull or underfull box. Limits: no print edition was requested, so this is a source review with a scratch build and not a print acceptance. tools/print-document still cannot export the edition.
